questions.question: Locomotion in ______ takes place with the help of a muscular foot.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Snails.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The snail is a very **slow-moving animal.**
 
• Like an **earthworm**, a snail too has a** liquid skeleton.**
 
• Snails have a** shell**, inside which they can hide to protect themselves from the heat of the sun and enemies.
 
• The shell is the **outer skeleton**, but it is **not made of bones**.
 
• For movement, **a thick structure and the head of the snail **come out of an opening in the shell.
 
• The thick structure is its** foot**, made of** strong muscles.**
 
• The** muscular foot produces wave-like movements** that push the **snail’s body forward.**
 
• A **trail of mucous** is left behind when the snail crawls.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Jellyfish**
 Jellyfish are animals of the phylum Cnidaria. They have no brain, heart, bones or eyes. They are made up of a smooth, bag-like body and tentacles armed with tiny, stinging cells.
 
 

 **Sea urchins**
 Sea urchins are the Class Echinoidea of the Phylum Echinodermata. These creatures are typically small, spiny, and round. They live in all the earth’s oceans, at depths ranging from the tide line to 15,000 feet.
 
 

 **Earthworms**
 Earthworms are classified in the phylum Annelida or Annelids. They are the main contributors to enriching and improving soil for plants, animals and even humans.

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding invertebrates from the options given below.

options.text: They possess a backbone and an internal skeleton.
They have radial or bilateral body symmetry.
They have a pair of solid nerve cords, situated ventrally and bearing segmentally arranged ganglia.
They have open circulatory system as there is no organisation in the distribution.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They possess a backbone and an internal skeleton**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Invertebrates do not possess a backbone or an internal skeleton.
 
• They exhibit either radial or bilateral body symmetry.
 
• They have a pair of solid nerve cords, situated ventrally and bearing segmentally arranged ganglia.
 
• They typically have an open circulatory system as there is no organization in the distribution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Invertebrates constitute a vast majority of animal species on Earth, covering groups such as insects, arachnids, mollusks, crustaceans, and more.
 
• Despite lacking a backbone, many invertebrates have specialized adaptations that allow them to thrive in diverse environments.
 
• The study of invertebrates is crucial for understanding ecological interactions, evolutionary biology, and the development of medical and technological innovations.
 
• Invertebrates play key roles in ecosystems, including pollination, decomposition, and serving as food for other animals.

questions.question: Which unicellular organism acquires food by a process in which cells absorb external material by engulfing it with the cell membrane?

__
 
• In **Amoeba**, the cell membrane help in** engulfing the food **during the process called **endocytosis.**
 
• Amoeba is **a unicellular organism that has the ability to change its shape**.
 
• They are usually found in** water bodies such as ponds, lakes, and slow-moving rivers.**

• Amoebae do not form a single** taxonomic group; **instead, they are found in every major **lineage of eukaryotic organisms.**** **

questions.question: How do the red algae reproduce vegetatively?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Fragmentation.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Red algae reproduce through ****Fragmentation**.

 
 
• **Red algae** is the numerous algae that **constitute the phylum Rhodophyta. **
 
• It contains a **red pigment** in addition to chlorophyll.
 
• The group includes **carrageen, dulse, and laver also called red seaweed.**
 
• It reproduces sexually as well as asexually.
 
• Asexual reproduction can occur through the production of spores and by vegetative means.
 
• It includes** fragmentation, cell division or propagules production.**
 
• **Fragmentation** is a method where **one fragment from an organism's body is broken due to external physical causes.**
 
• **Each fragment then grows into different individuals.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fission**

 
 
• **​**The type of asexual reproduction in which a **microorganism splits in two equal halves is called as binary fission.**
 
• **Binary fission occurs in Amoeba.**
 
• The cells which split during binary fission have the potential to grow to the size of the original one.
 
 
 
• **Spore Formation**
 
 
• ​**Spore formation **is a method of** asexual reproduction.**
 
• Plants like** ferns, moss, and fungi **reproduce by this method.
 
• **Spores are unicellular reproductive bodies** present in sacs called **sporangia.**
 
• When spores mature sporangia burst and spores are carried to a different location by air, wind, and water.
 
 
 
• **Cutting**
 
 
• **Cutting** is a type of asexual reproduction.
 
• **​**A cutting is a **vegetative plant part.**
 
• It is severed from the parent plant in order to regenerate itself, thereby forming a whole new plant.

questions.question: Which of the following microscopic cells are of an amoeboid shape with a distinctive central membrane?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**White blood cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **White blood cells** are of an amoeboid shape with a distinctive central membrane.
 
• The **amoeboid** shape of WBCs helps them to **squeeze out** through the **capillary wall**.
 
• White blood cells help in **defence mechanisms** for our body.
 
• They play a major role in** putting away foreign particles**.
 
• At the site of infection, white blood cells accumulate to **destroy pathogens.**
 
• Their **amoeboid shape** assists them to squeeze through blood capillaries and at the same time their pseudopodia help to kill pathogens by the process of phagocytosis. 
 
• They change their shape in order to **sink bacteria and separate invaders** in the body in order to protect the body against diseases and infections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Nerve cells **(neurones) are 'excitable' cells which can transduce a variety of stimuli into electrical signals, continuously sending information about the external and internal environment (in the form of sequences of action potentials) to the central nervous system (CNS).
 
• **Guard cells** are pairs of epidermal cells that control gas diffusion by regulating the opening and closure of stomatal pores. Guard cells, like other types of plant cells, are surrounded by a three-dimensional, extracellular network of polysaccharide-based wall polymers.
 
• **Red blood cells **contain a protein called haemoglobin, which carries oxygen from the lungs to all parts of the body. Checking the number of red blood cells in the blood is usually part of a complete blood cell (CBC) test. A type of blood cell that is made in the bone marrow and found in the blood.

questions.question: Which group of animals has a segmented spinal column together with a few primitive forms in which the backbone is represented by a notochord?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vertebrata**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vertebrata** is the group of animals that have a segmented spinal column.
 
• This group includes not only advanced organisms with a developed backbone but also some primitive forms in which the backbone is represented by a notochord.
 
• The notochord is a flexible rod-like structure that forms the main support of the body in these primitive organisms.
 
• Examples of vertebrates include mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fish.
 
• The presence of a segmented spinal column is a key characteristic that differentiates vertebrates from other animal groups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vertebrates** are part of the phylum Chordata, which is characterized by the presence of a notochord at some stage of development.
 
• The notochord is replaced by the vertebral column in most adult vertebrates, providing more structural support and protection for the spinal cord.
 
• Other distinguishing features of vertebrates include a well-developed brain, a closed circulatory system, and an endoskeleton made of bone or cartilage.
 
• The evolutionary development of the vertebral column has allowed vertebrates to become highly adaptable and occupy a wide range of ecological niches.
 
• Vertebrates are the most complex and diverse group of animals, with over 66,000 species described to date.

questions.question: In ruminants like cattle, bacteria present in ________ helps in digestion of cellulose.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rumen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In ruminants like cattle, bacteria present in the rumen (the largest compartment of the stomach) play a crucial role in the digestion of cellulose.
 
• The rumen is a fermentation chamber where complex carbohydrates, such as cellulose from plant material, are broken down by microbial fermentation.
 
• Bacteria in the rumen possess cellulolytic enzymes that break down cellulose into simpler forms that can be further digested and utilized by the ruminant host.
 
• This symbiotic relationship between ruminants and rumen bacteria allows them to efficiently extract nutrients from plant-based diets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In honey bees, males are haploid and females are diploid.**
 
• **Males (drones)** develop from unfertilized eggs and possess only **one set of chromosomes**.
 
• Females (workers and queens) develop from fertilized eggs and possess two sets of chromosomes.
 
• This is an example of a genetic system known as **haplodiploidy**.
 
• The haplodiploid system determines the sex of the offspring based on the number of chromosome sets they receive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Haplodiploidy** is a common genetic system in several insect orders, including Hymenoptera (bees, ants, and wasps).
 
• In haplodiploid species, the sex determination mechanism can influence social structure and behavior, particularly in eusocial species like honey bees.
 
• **Queens can control the sex of their offspring by choosing whether to fertilize an egg**.
 
• This system allows for a high degree of relatedness among workers, which can promote cooperative behaviors.

questions.question: Which among the following pairs of 'animal - phylum of animal kingdom they belong' is incorrect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Liver __**fluke - Nematoda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Liver Fluke - 

 
 
• The scientific name of liver fluke is Fasciola hepatica.
 
• The life history of liver fluke involves two hosts (Digenetic parasitic).
 
• Primary host - Sheep and goat
 
• Secondary host - Garden snail (Planorbis, Lymnea)
 
• Liver fluke belongs to the **phylum Platyhelminthes, not Nematoda.**
 
• Liver fluke is a parasitic flatworm that infects the liver of its primary host, which is usually a sheep or goat.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sycon - Porifera**

 
 
• Sycon is a sponge that belongs to the phylum Porifera.
 
• The common name of the Sycon is Crown Sponge.
 
• All sponges have a canal system that consists of the Ostia, spongocoel, and osculum.
 
• Canal system is one of the most important features of sponges.
 
• The canal system is a network of canals that connect the spongocoel to the outside via ostia.
 
• It helps in nutrition, respiration, and excretion processes.
 
 
 
• **Prawns - Arthropoda**
 
 
• Prawn is a common name for small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs (i.e.** a member of the order decapoda**), some of which can be eaten. 
 
• They belong to the kingdom Animalia and order **Arthropoda**.
 
 
 
• **​Starfish - Echinodermata**
 
 
• Starfish belongs to the phylum Echinodermata group.
 
• Echinodermata are so named owing to their spiny skin (from the Greek “echinos” meaning “spiny” and “dermos” meaning “skin”).
 
• Echinodermata are exclusively marine organisms. Sea stars, sea cucumbers, sea urchins, sand dollars, and brittle stars are all examples of echinoderms.

questions.question: Animals of which phylum have jointed legs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arthropoda.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arthropoda** is a group of invertebrate animals having an exoskeleton, a segmented body and jointed legs.
 
• Their body consists of segments with a pair of appendages.
 
• Their reproduction occurs by internal fertilization (terrestrial species) and internal or external fertilization (aquatic species).
 
• They have an open circulatory system.
 
• Types of Arthropods –
 
 
• Insects: Ants, Aphids, Butterflies, Grasshoppers, Termites, and etc.
 
• Arachnids: Scorpion, Mites, Spiders
 
• Crustacean: Crabs, Fish, Lobsters, Shrimp, and etc.
 
 
 
• Their evolution dates back to the Cambrian period.
 
• They are a source of food for humans.
 
• They are pollinators of crops.
 
• Some species spread diseases to humans, livestock, and crops.
 
• Largest phylum of invertebrate animals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mollusca** – 2nd largest phylum of invertebrate animals mostly found in marine and freshwater having the soft body divided into head, visceral mass, muscular foot, and mantle. Examples: Snail, Octopus, Squid, Oyster, Clams, and etc.
 
• **Nematoda:** bilaterally symmetrical, elongate and tapered at both ends; an important role in nutrient recycling in the soil feed. They cause diseases such as Ascariasis, Enterobiasis, Filariasis, and etc. Examples: Ascarids, Worms
 
• **Echinodermata:** marine animals having a star-like appearance, Echinoderms (Phylum Echinodermata) are a diverse, exclusively marine group of invertebrates.
 
 
• Examples: Starfish, Sea urchins, Crinoids, etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fa1a55bb54b9cadef590bd50eb3bd64b2a36de8895342e9c1eff2382db946414.png] 

 
• All arthropods lay eggs except Scorpion who directly give birth to young.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of Phylum – Annelida?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An example of the **phylum Annelida** is the **earthworm**.
 
• **Earthworms** belong to the class** Clitellata** within the **phylum Annelida.**
 
• They are segmented worms characterized by their long, **cylindrical bodies** divided into **numerous repeated segments**.
 
• **Earthworms **are commonly found in soil and play a vital role in the ecosystem by enhancing soil fertility through their burrowing and decomposition activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Hookworms** are** parasitic worms** that infect the s**mall intestine of humans and other animals.**

 
 
• There are two main species of hookworm that commonly infect humans: **Ancylostoma duodenale and Necator americanus.**
 
• These worms are named for their hook-like mouthparts, which they use to attach to the intestinal lining and feed on blood.
 
• **Hookworm infection** occurs when a person comes into contact with contaminated soil or feces that contain hookworm larvae.
 
• The larvae can penetrate **the skin, usually through bare feet, and migrate through the bloodstream to reach the lungs.**
 
• From there, they are coughed up and swallowed, eventually reaching the small intestine where they mature into adult worms. Adult hookworms then attach to the intestinal wall and start feeding on blood, which can lead to iron deficiency anemia.
 
 
 
• **Filaria worms, also known as filarial nematodes, are a group of parasitic worms that belong to the family Filariidae.**
 
 
• These worms are responsible for causing a group of diseases known as **filariasis or lymphatic filariasis.**
 
• **Filariasis** is a tropical and subtropical disease that affects millions of people worldwide, particularly in regions such as Africa, Southeast Asia, and the Pacific Islands.
 
 
 
• **Roundworms, also known as nematodes, are a diverse group of worms that belong to the phylum Nematoda.**
 
• They are among the most common animals on Earth and can be found in a wide range of** environments, including soil, freshwater, and marine habitats**.
 
• Some roundworms are free-living, while others are parasitic and can infect **plants, animals, and humans.**

questions.question: What is the cottony growth over a stale and moist bread known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fungi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Fungi** are a kingdom of usually multicellular, eukaryotic organisms that are heterotrophs (cannot produce their own food).
 
• They play a crucial role in the ecosystem by decomposing organic matter and recycling nutrients.
 
• Fungi can thrive in a variety of environments, particularly where there is decaying organic matter, such as stale and moist bread.
 
• The cottony growth seen on stale and moist bread is a result of fungal spores landing on the bread and proliferating under favorable conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fungi**:

 
 
• Fungi include microorganisms such as yeasts and molds, as well as the more familiar mushrooms.
 
• They are vital decomposers in the ecosystem, breaking down organic matter and returning nutrients to the soil.
 
• Unlike plants, fungi do not perform photosynthesis; they obtain their nutrients through absorption.
 
• Many fungi form symbiotic relationships with plants, such as mycorrhizae, which aid in plant nutrient uptake.
 
 
 
• **Lichens**:
 
 
• Lichens are a symbiotic association between a fungus and an alga or cyanobacterium.
 
• They are known for their ability to colonize harsh environments, such as bare rocks.
 
• Lichens are important bioindicators of environmental health and air quality.
 
 
 
• **Algae**:
 
 
• Algae are a diverse group of photosynthetic organisms found in a variety of aquatic environments.
 
• They range from single-celled microorganisms to large multicellular forms like seaweeds.
 
• Algae play a key role in aquatic ecosystems by producing oxygen and serving as the base of the food chain.
 
 
 
• **Bacteria**:
 
 
• Bacteria are single-celled microorganisms that can be found in almost every habitat on Earth.
 
• They play essential roles in processes like nitrogen fixation, decomposition, and fermentation.
 
• Some bacteria are beneficial to humans, while others can cause diseases.
 
 

This code provides a detailed explanation of the correct option (Fungi) and additional information on related terminologies such as Lichens, Algae, and Bacteria

questions.question: The body of animals of the phylum Protozoa, such as Paramecium, Amoeba, Euglena, shows ________ grade organisation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**protoplasmic.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Protozoa is a phylum having **unicellular heterotrophs**. It comes under Kingdom Protista.
 
• A protozoan body consists of only a mass of protoplasm, so they are called acellular or non-cellular animals. Grade of organization: **protoplasmic grade of organization**.
 
• **Single-cell performs all the vital activities thus the single cell acts** like a whole body. The body** of protozoa is either naked or covered by a pellicle.**
 
• Protozoa can be divided into four phyla based on their locomotion: **Mastigophora, Sarcodina, Ciliophora, and Sporozoa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b1149550084fd4e895543d9f40fb390a035a2a2e0b6f723b3f1bed13d404409.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tissue-organ**_​ The organ level of organization is **when two or more tissues work together for a specific function**. For example, **the bladder consists of an inner lining of epithelial tissue, bound by various connective tissues to (smooth) muscle.**
 
• Most organisms have functional parts with five levels: **cells, tissues, organs, organ systems and whole organisms**.
 
• "Cellular organization" is **the defining property in living organisms.**

questions.question: What components are often called the building blocks of the body that play a vital role in helping to repair and strengthen muscle tissues after exercise?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Proteins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Proteins**

 
 
• Of all macromolecules,** proteins have the widest diversity of functions and are one of the most abundant organic molecules **in biological systems.
 
• Because there are **20 different chemically unique amino acids that combine to produce lengthy chains of proteins**, the functions of proteins are **extremely diverse**.
 
• Protein is essential to **our diet because it helps our bodies create and repair new cells**.
 
• For children, teenagers, and pregnant women, protein is also crucial for **growth and development**.
 
• Consumed protein is **converted to amino acids by the body** and then absorbed.
 
• It is utilised in the **development of muscles and organs, production of hormones and antibodies, storage of fat, and production of energy**.
 
• Proteins are commonly called as the building blocks of the body because they play a vital role in helping to repair and strengthen muscle tissues after exercise.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Animal products** such as **meats, milk, fish, and eggs are rich sources of protein**, they can also be found in **plant-based foods** like **some grains, beans, soy, legumes, nut kinds of butter, and legumes**.
 
• **Carbohydrates**
 
 
• **Carbohydrates also called carbs** are one of the** three primary nutrients included in foods and beverages**, along with proteins and fats.
 
• The body converts carbohydrates to **glucose**. The primary **fuel for your body's cells, tissues, and organs is glucose, also known as blood sugar**.
 
• **Grains, such as bread, cereals, and rice**, are typical sources of carbs.
 
• **Providing energy to all of the body's cells** is the main function of carbs
 
 
 
• **​Micronutrients**
 
 
• **Vitamins and minerals **that our body needs in **very small amounts are known as micronutrients**.
 
• However, they have a c**rucial impact on a body's health**, and a lack of any one of them can result in serious, even li**fe-threatening illnesses**.
 
 
 
• **Fats**
 
 
• Fat is the **primary energy storage type in the body** and is used as a fuel source by the body.
 
• A **moderate amount of fat is required in the diet for optimal health** since it performs numerous other vital activities in the body.
 
• Food contains a variety of fats, such as **monounsaturated, polyunsaturated, and saturated fats**. 
 
• **Butter, oil, nuts, meat, fish, and various dairy products **are a few examples of foods that include fats.
